audit_result.proof_trace: The RLS policy 'Allow read access for all users' on attendance.temp_registrations uses USING (true) with no role restriction and no column exclusion, granting the anon role unrestricted SELECT access to all rows including qr_token. The fix migration (20260317000001) preserves and explicitly reinforces this SELECT grant without adding any expiry filter or column-level restriction. Since qr_token is the sole bearer credential for the card-ID-to-user-account linking flow (completeRegistration), and the kiosk Realtime subscription does not require enumerating all tokens (it already knows the token it generated), neither disjunct of the property holds.
audit_result.attack_scenario: An unauthenticated attacker sends GET /rest/v1/temp_registrations?select=qr_token,card_id to the Supabase PostgREST endpoint and retrieves all active QR tokens; the attacker then authenticates as any account and visits /register/STOLEN_TOKEN, causing completeRegistration to link their auth identity to the victim's card_id and enabling them to forge attendance records as the victim.

PROP-0000-create-inv-003.text: temp_registrations qr_token must not be readable by anon role to prevent token theft.
PROP-0000-create-inv-003.assertion: policy(temp_registrations, anon, SELECT).columns NOT INCLUDES qr_token OR policy restricts expired rows
